results.title: How to Use
results.content:
## Use CALL-E on other coding agents and AI assistants

CALL-E is designed to work wherever modern AI workflows happen. You can use it directly inside ChatGPT, or connect it to coding agents and desktop AI assistants. [...] CALL-E can also support real-time reminders when a phone call is more reliable than a message.

Example prompt:

> “Call me immediately if there is a transaction anomaly or account risk event.”

This is useful for financial analysts, traders, gaming operators, or operations teams who need fast phone-based alerts.

> 👍_Note: Please refer to section, “Use CALL-E on other coding agents and AI assistants”, for more information._

## Where CALL-E is currently available

CALL-E currently supports calls in selected countries, including the United States.

Some countries are not currently supported, including Kenya and Vietnam.

> Note: Availability may change, so check inside CALL-E before placing a call. If you need assistance, please contact the CALL-E support team at support@heycall-e.com. [...] ## Tips for better CALL-E prompts

Give CALL-E:

1. Who to call and what number (including the country code)  
2. The goal of the call  
3. Key details like date, time, order number, or phone number  
4. What to do if no one answers  
5. What information to report back

A strong prompt looks like this:

> “Call Bella’s Bistro to book a table for 2 people this Saturday at 7 PM. Ask for a window seat. Use my phone number for the reservation. If they do not answer, leave a voicemail and ask them to call me back.”

CALL-E works best when your request is specific, simple, and outcome-focused.

results.title: I built a phone number you can call and argue with an AI — here's the part nobody tells you | Wanjohi Christopher
results.content:
First, a quick glossary so the rest reads clean:

 PSTN: the regular phone network. Actual calls, not app-to-app.
 DID: the phone number people dial.
 Telnyx: my telephony provider. It bridges the phone call to my server.
 Webhook: Telnyx HTTP-POSTs my server when something happens on the call.
 Media stream: Telnyx sends me the raw audio, live, instead of a transcript.
 STT / TTS: speech→text and text→speech.
 VAD: voice activity detection. Figuring out when the caller stopped talking.

## Attempt 1: let the phone company do the hard part

The obvious first move is to let Telnyx handle speech. They have an API for it. The loop looks clean on a whiteboard: [...] One transcription engine returns `200 OK` and then sends zero transcription events. Forever. No error. It just silently does nothing.
 The moment I added a config option to pick a better transcription model, the whole thing went quiet again. Same `200 OK`, still no events.
 Their built-in "AI assistant" feature can only be started once per call, so you can't use it to drive a turn-by-turn conversation with your own logic.
 And the speech recognition keeps transcribing the agent's own voice as if the caller said it, so you have to choreograph exactly when you start and stop listening around when you're talking. [...] ## What it costs, and what I'd do next

Every turn logs its budget: `STT time / AI time / TTS time`. That single log line is the most useful thing I added, because on a phone call latency is the product. A 4-second silence after someone asks a question feels broken even if the answer is perfect. In my setup, the LLM call dominated that budget, which points at the obvious next moves: stream the TTS so the caller hears the first words while the rest is still generating, and start synthesizing speech from the model's tokens as they arrive instead of waiting for the full reply.

# AI call center: how AI voice agents handle support calls, and where people stay on the line



byYevhenii Nesterenko

Head of CoMarketing

15views

An AI voice agent handling a support call and passing it to a person for an exception

An AI call center answers support calls with AI voice agents. The agent understands what the caller says, checks the account, follows your policies, takes the action, and passes the call to a person when it can't finish the job. The phone line stays, and the AI picks up first.

Callers still choose the phone. In Deloitte Digital's 2026 survey of 3,000 consumers, people were twice as likely to prefer phone over self-service for simple issues, and 5.5 times as likely when the issue felt complex (Deloitte Digital). [...] ## What is an AI call center?

An AI call center is a phone support operation where AI voice agents answer first and resolve the routine share of calls, and people handle the rest with the context the AI already gathered. An AI voice agent is the software on the line. A call runs through it in three steps: [...] | Call reason | Can the caller fix it alone? | Cost of a wrong answer | Who should take it |
 ---  --- |
| Opening hours, delivery times | Yes | Low | Help center or AI voice agent |
| Invoice copy, appointment change | Yes, with account access | Low | AI voice agent |
| Address change, plan change | No, needs an action | Medium | AI voice agent, with verification and read-back |
| Double charge within policy | No, needs a refund | Medium | AI voice agent, with verification and read-back |
| Failed delivery before an event, locked account while travelling | No, and it's urgent | High | AI voice agent for the first steps, a person for any exception |
| Complaint, bereavement, refund outside policy | No | High | A person, with the AI's summary |
